# S409 — Check commands: a quoted | is not a pipe, and the implementer may run rg

The Check classifier that sorts Check commands into implementer-runnable and orchestrator-only reads quotes the way ork's own check runner does, so a `|`, `&`, `;`, `<` or `>` inside single or double quotes no longer makes a command compound. Both implementer presets (`go` and `python`) gain `Bash(rg *)`, so the built-in default allowlist covers read-only `rg` searches.

**Findings:** 2026-11-17: the spec check flagged orchestrator-only Check lines on S402, S396, S397, S390, S332 and S388, the same question as adj 249, 255, 256 and 259. Two causes: `checkCommandRunnable` (`internal/engine/brief.go:546-552`) treats any `;|&<>` or backtick or `$` as a compound command even inside quotes, so `go test ./internal/daemon -run 'A|B' -v` is orchestrator-only, while `plainCheckSyntax` (`internal/engine/brief.go:486-522`), which decides what ork itself runs, already accepts a quoted `|`. And `ImplementerPreset` (`internal/engine/perm.go:45-71`) has no `rg` entry, so every `rg -n ...` Check line is orchestrator-only. · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

Owner rule (2026-11-17): a deterministic step done regularly is code, not a model call or a hand step. Each spec check of a slice whose Check uses `go test -run 'A|B'` or `rg` raises an owner question about orchestrator-only lines (adj 249, 255, 256, 259, and six more slices on 2026-11-17). The commands are plain and safe; the classifier and the allowlist are what make them orchestrator-only.

Owner decisions (2026-11-17): the implementer presets allow `Bash(rg *)` [launch.allowlist-rg, adj 455; extends adj 75]. ork is fixed in code first, and S402, S396, S397, S390, S332 and S388 wait until this slice lands [checks.implementer-runnable, adj 456].

## Implement

1. In `checkCommandRunnable`, replace the two `strings.ContainsAny(command, ";|&<>\n`$")` tests with a helper that reports shell syntax outside quotes, built on the same scan as `plainCheckSyntax` (single quotes literal; inside double quotes only `$` and backtick count). A command with unquoted `;|&<>`, a newline, `$` or a backtick keeps today's rule (needs an explicit whole-command allowlist form).
2. Add `Bash(rg *)` to the shared tail in `ImplementerPreset`, after the `adj` entries, so both presets get it.
3. Update `docs/design.md` (default allowlist list and the S265 preset paragraph) and `docs/guide.md:255` to name `Bash(rg *)`, citing `launch.allowlist-rg` (adj 455).
4. Add an Unreleased CHANGELOG entry with `slicer changelog add`.

## Check

Acceptance criteria:
- A Check line with a quoted pipe, such as go test -run 'A|B', is classified implementer-runnable in the role brief.
- A Check line with an unquoted pipe, redirect, ';' or '&&' stays orchestrator-only unless an allowlist form names the whole command.
- An rg Check line with paths inside the worktree is implementer-runnable under the built-in default and both presets.
- A spec check of S402 no longer lists 'go test ./internal/daemon -run ...' as orchestrator-only.
- docs/design.md and docs/guide.md list Bash(rg *) in the presets.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/engine -run CheckCommandRunnable -v`
- `go test ./internal/engine -run ImplementerPreset -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` must print nothing.
